dialogue.Introduction: Welcome to my general store! Everything here is for sale, and most of it is a bargain. Most of it.$h
dialogue.Mon: Good morning, @! Looking for supplies? I have seeds, bait, and a few suspicious potions that fell off a goblin cart.$h
dialogue.Tue: Tuesday is the slowest day for trade. Nobody wants to buy anything while the farm is still wet with dew.#$b#So I count my coins twice. Then I count them again.$h
dialogue.Wed: Hello, @. Did you know a Dryad once tried to sell me a sapling for three gold? I told her I would take ten, and she laughed at me.$u
dialogue.Thu: Ah, @! Business is booming, thanks to the goblin army clearing out the hills. Their loot is worth a fortune, provided you do not mind the smell.$h
dialogue.Fri: The Demolitionist came in again yesterday asking for more gunpowder. I sold him a crate, of course. Business is business, even when it blows things up.$h
dialogue.Sat: Saturday means the saloon is full and my store is empty. The Tavernkeep says that is because I am too expensive. Nonsense, I am simply priced correctly.$a
dialogue.Sun: Sunday is a day of rest, but I keep the shutters half open. A good merchant never truly sleeps. Well, not since the Wall of Flesh incident anyway.$s
dialogue.Mon4: @, you have been a loyal customer for a while now. I have started saving the good stock for you. Do not tell the others, they would be jealous.$h
dialogue.Tue4: Between us, the coins are not the best part of this job. Meeting folk from every corner of the Terraria world is what keeps me going.$h
dialogue.Wed4: My grandfather ran a shop like this one. He sold rope and lanterns to miners heading into the mines. I still keep his brass scale on the counter.$s
dialogue.Thu4: I do not usually say this to customers, but I am glad you came to Pelican Town. The valley feels a little more alive since the Terraria folk moved in.$h
dialogue.Fri4: Every Friday I restock the shelves from the caravan that comes through the Calico Desert. Those camel drivers are the worst haggling partners in the valley.$a
dialogue.Sat4: If you ever need a discount, just ask nicely. Nicely and with a smile. I do have a soft spot for a farmer who smiles.$h
dialogue.Sun4: Sundays are when I sit back and count my savings. Half of it goes to the store, and the other half goes into a little cottage by the sea someday.$h
dialogue.Mon8: I will tell you a secret, @. When I first came to this valley I was so scared I could barely speak. Selling things was the only way I knew how to make friends.$s
dialogue.Tue8: You know what scares me most? Not the bosses, not the blood moons. It is the day the store is empty and nobody needs anything from me.$s
dialogue.Wed8: Thank you for always coming by, @. Most folks only shop when they need something. You visit just to talk, and that means more to me than all the gold in my till.$h
dialogue.Thu8: Sometimes I dream I am selling wares to the cosmic folk beneath the Moon Lord. They always ask for a discount. Always.$u
dialogue.Fri8: When I was a boy my mother told me a good deal makes both people smile. I have not forgotten that, even when the Clothier and I argue over prices.$h
dialogue.Sat8: I am glad you are my friend, @. Honestly, I think I would have closed the shop years ago without someone to talk to on quiet afternoons like this.$l
dialogue.Sun8: If you ever need anything, come to me first. I will look after you, and I will only charge you a little. Do not tell the Tavernkeep I said that.$h
dialogue.Mon2: Oh, a customer! Do you want the good bait or the cheap bait? The cheap bait is for the Angler, he is very picky.$h
dialogue.Tue2: Please keep your hands off the top shelf, @. The Party Girl once hid a whole barrel of confetti up there. We are still finding it in the carts.$a
dialogue.Wed2: The Guide walked in yesterday asking for directions to the Dungeon. I sold him a map, of course. Well, I sold him an old wrapping paper and called it a map.$h
dialogue.Thu2: The Golfer keeps buying golf balls from me. Hundreds of them. I do not think he has ever once hit one.$u
dialogue.Fri2: Every buyer thinks they are getting the best price. Clever buyers know they are getting exactly the price I wanted.$h
dialogue.Sat2: The Goblin Tinkerer keeps asking me for gears, and he always leaves without paying. We have a truce, I suppose.$s
dialogue.Sun2: A fine day for shopping, @. The sun is out and the valley looks lovely. Perfect for selling something to a farmer who has been standing here too long.$h
dialogue.Tue6: The Demolitionist asked me for thirty bundles of dynamite once. He does not own a single blast-proof wall. I do not ask questions, I simply ask for payment first.$h
dialogue.Thu6: @, you know the mines are dangerous. I stock extra lanterns for you, just in case. Not because I care. Because they sell well.$h
dialogue.Sat6: When the Party Girl throws a party the whole town crowds into my shop for snacks. I make a fortune. I also sweep up a mess. Mostly I make a fortune.$h
dialogue.Fri10: @, I have been keeping an eye on your stock. You work harder than anyone I know. If you ever need a loan, you will have my first offer.$h
dialogue.summer_Wed: The summer heat is terrible for stock. Keep the cheese in the cellar, @, unless you want to be selling moldy wheels for a month.$a
dialogue.winter_Fri8: It is cold outside, @, but the store is warm. Come in, have a seat, and I will tell you about the good old days when this place was half the size.$h
dialogue.fall_Tue4: Fall harvest is my favorite time. Everyone in the valley brings me their best crops, and I am always happy to buy the best ones.$h
dialogue.summer_Sun: A lovely summer Sunday, @. The beach is busy and the saloon is loud. I do not mind it. Loud customers buy loud things.$h
dialogue.winter_Mon: Winter is hard on business. Folks stay indoors and only buy what they absolutely need. Heat lamps and wool sell like crazy this time of year, though.$h
dialogue.fall_Thu: This fall I plan to clear out the old stock and make room for the new goods the Terraria traders have promised. Worth every coin, I assure you.$h
dialogue.spring_Sat: Spring is a fresh start. New seeds arrive at the store, and every farmer comes in with a hopeful look. Let us make this year the best one yet, @.$h
dialogue.spring_Fri6: The spring rain is wonderful for my crops but terrible for my cellar. I have buckets everywhere. Sometimes I think the store leaks more than the sky.$s
dialogue.fall_15: Halfway through fall and the shelves are finally looking full. Do not let me catch you buying the last pumpkin seeds, @. Those belong to me.$h

rainy: Rain on the roof and not a single customer in sight. Come in out of the wet, @, and I will tell you about the time the goblins tried to sell me a leaky bucket.$h

situations.eye: The Eye of Cthulhu is finally gone, @. I sold a dozen lenses to its fans before they stopped staring. Business as usual, but quieter.$h
situations.evilBoss: The Eater of Worlds and the Brain of Cthulhu, I do not care which. Whatever crawled out of the ground is gone, and my shelves are fuller for it.$u
situations.skeletron: The dungeon is open, @, and the Old Man is free at last. The Clothier was very upset about that, so I sold him a bandage. He will be fine.$h
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is down. Honey everywhere! I bought every jar the bees left behind and sold it all before lunch.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh fell and hardmode began. The Hallow glows and the monsters are meaner, so my prices just went up. Blame the monsters, not me.$s
situations.mechs: One of those mechanical bosses was destroyed last night. I heard the noise from my cellar and sold all my spare gears by morning.$u
situations.plantera: Plantera is defeated and the jungle temple is open. The jungle folk want seeds in return. I told them my prices are firm, but I do have a nice deal on bamboo.$h
situations.golem: The Golem is finally gone. The lihzahrd temple is quiet now. I miss the traders, but I do not miss the traps.$s
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is defeated and the celestial pillars glow in the sky. A stargazer paid me in fallen stars yesterday. Strange currency, but it sparkles.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is gone, @. The whole valley cheered. I tried to sell the crowd some souvenirs, and they bought every single one. Wonderful.$h
situations.goblins: The goblin army was repelled last night. Their leader ran off with my best shovel. I have decided to call that an unpaid debt.$a
situations.pirates: The pirates tried to raid the docks but they were sent packing. They left behind a chest of gold coins. I do not trust pirates, but I trust their gold.$h
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion came out of the snow and we pushed them back. I sold a whole crate of warm blankets. Best winter sales I have ever had.$h
situations.martians: The Martians came with lasers and flying saucers, and we sent them home. I wonder if they would like a discount on fuel. Probably not.$u
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night, @. Keep your doors locked. The zombies bought nothing, which is very rude of them, and I stayed up counting coins.$s
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark yesterday during the eclipse and every shopper ran home. Nobody bought a thing. I spent the afternoon staring at the sky and sweeping floors.$s
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today, @! I have stocked extra snacks and party hats. I will charge double, of course. That is what parties are for.$h

festivals.spring13: Egg Festival! I have hidden the best eggs in the valley for the contest. Well, I hid them in my shop. Do not tell the children.$h
festivals.spring24: Flower Dance. I always pick the prettiest flower for my dance partner, though I usually have to sell it to them first.$h
festivals.summer11: The Luau! I have added a crate of my finest cheese to the community soup. It is a generous donation, I promise, and not at all a way to win the big prize.$h
festivals.summer28: The Dance of the Moonlight Jellies. I stand on the beach and watch the jellies glow. They do not buy anything, but they are very pretty to look at.$h
festivals.fall16: Stardew Valley Fair. The grange displays are wonderful this year, but my own display is better. Look at those pumpkins! Priced to sell.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve. The haunted maze is terrifying. A ghost tried to haggle with me in there. Honestly, I think he won.$u
festivals.winter8: Festival of Ice. The ice fishing contest is on, and the Angler is already complaining about the cold. I sold him a warm hat for his troubles.$h
festivals.winter25: Feast of the Winter Star. I have a gift for you under the counter, @. It is a secret gift, so do not look yet. Not until we exchange them properly.$h

loved.text: Oh! Now that is what I call a valuable item. I will treasure it, and I will know exactly what it is worth.$h

liked.text: Nice, very nice. That is a fine piece of merchandise. I could sell it, but I think I will keep it.$h

neutral.text: Hmm. Not bad, not great. I will find a spot on the shelf for it, eventually.

disliked.text: Ugh, junk! Is this from a goblin cart? I am not taking that as a gift, friend. Take it back to the scrap pile.$a

hated.text: Are you trying to insult me? That is trash. I have a reputation to protect, @, and this does not help one bit.$a

help: Help! Guard! Somebody call the guard, or a cheaper one!
This is robbery! Well, it will be if it eats me!
Is that thing a customer? No? Then I am leaving!
thanks: I owe you a discount, @. Please do not tell the others.$h
@, you saved my skin, and my skin is worth at least three gold!$h
battle: Stay back! I have... a knife! It is a small knife!
For the store! For the ledgers! Ahh, AHH, AHHH!
I shall defend my inventory! Mostly with this knife!
courage.hurt: Ow. That knife bounced off a slime and hit me in the shin. My pride is bruised too.$s

danger.boss: A boss is loose out there? The shop is closed. Yes, closed. Ask me tomorrow.$a
danger.invasion: Goblins, pirates, frost, Martians! Every army in the valley is at my door. Prices doubled from fear.$a
danger.pumpkinMoon: The pumpkins are walking and the scarecrows look angry. I am counting my coins under the bed.$a
danger.frostMoon: The frost moon is out, and the cold is coming for my inventory. Hide the potions, quickly!$a
danger.eclipse: The sun went dark and the monsters came out. I am staying behind the counter until it passes.$a
danger.bloodMoon: Blood moon tonight. Lock the door, bar the windows, and do not look at the sky, friend.$a

events.after: Don't tell anyone about my secret stash, alright?

steps.say: Oh! @, you startled me. I was just counting today's takings.$u
Forty-one gold... forty-two... Hm? Why yes, I always count twice.#$b#A merchant who trusts his first count is a poor merchant.$h

answers.reply: Ha! Perhaps. Friends do get the best prices.$h
Greedy? I prefer the word thrifty.$a

steps.say: Here. Something to keep your own coin safe. Every adventurer needs one.$h

events.after: Keep your eyes open for bargains on the road, friend.

steps.say: @! Just the customer I was hoping to see. Have you noticed the square is missing a bench? I have been meaning to sell one.$h
Between us, the Terraria folk keep wandering in with coins that are not from this world.#$b#A goblin tried to pay me with a rusty spoon. I could not believe my eyes.$u
Anyway, I have seeds on sale this spring. Half price for the first ten customers, and you are very near the front of the line.$h
Do not tell the others about the discount.$s

events.after: The Tavernkeep still owes me a drink. Do not let him forget it.

steps.say: Ah, @! Come, sit. The Tavernkeep and I were just arguing about who owes whom a drink.$h
Owes? You owe me three months of rent for that crate of Pale Ale.$a
Rent is a dirty word, friend. Ask our farmer here, they know a good deal when they see one.$h

answers.reply: Ha! A good judge of character, @.$h
Traitor. Nobody ever votes for the coin.$a

steps.say: Hmph. Fine. The next round is on me then, if only to spite him.$h
Well, that is one round of goodwill. Now I need a second.$h

events.after: Thank you for listening. It is nice to say it out loud sometimes.

steps.say: @, you are still here. Come in, I was just closing up for the night.$h
I never told you why I took this store, did I? My grandfather built it, and when the goblins came I was the only one left who knew the books.$s
I thought I would sell it when the Terraria folk moved in. Instead I found friends I did not expect.$h

answers.reply: Good. So am I, friend. Truly.$l
Ha! Then I will make sure the discounts stay good.$h

steps.say: Now go home, @. Morning comes early, and I have shelves to fill.$h

events.after: I'm still thinking about your farm. Such a lovely spread of crops.

steps.say: Look at this farm, @! Every row is straight and every crop is glowing. I would sell you the whole field if it were not already yours.$h
You know, I used to count coins. Now I count friends, and you are the best of them.$l

steps.question: Want to be my partner in business?

answers.reply: Splendid! I will bring the ledger. You bring the crops.$h
Fair enough. The offer will still be on the counter.$h

steps.say: For you, a little gift. This ruby has been waiting in my drawer for a special friend.$h
